the design of a search engine infrastructure that can support generic relational operations, including indexes, on very large datasets, while retaining the scalability of MapReduce.

we propose Traverse as a primitive for MapReduce Merge to support tree indexes, and to improve efficiency in the execution of map, reduce and merge operations.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have extended the scope of MapReduce to include tree indexing and traversing.
we are extending the MapReduce framework to support indexing and traversing of large datasets.

we show that indexing is feasible in Map Reduce Merge and that the indexing process can be made efficient by the Traverse operation.
we can build a generic framework for indexing, traversing, and processing large datasets on the MapReduce infrastructure, which is the foundation of most search engines today.
